video_title: The Planet Where Seasons Last 42 Years?! (Uranus's Bizarre Tilt)
script: Imagine a planet where summer lasts 42 years, and then winter lasts another 42 years! Welcome to Uranus, the solar system's oddball that spins almost completely on its side. With an axial tilt of nearly 98 degrees, Uranus rolls through space like a tumbleweed. This extreme tilt means that for almost half its orbit, one pole is constantly bathed in sunlight while the other is plunged into absolute darkness. That's 42 Earth years of endless day, followed by 42 years of unending night! Scientists believe a massive collision billions of years ago literally knocked Uranus sideways. This ancient catastrophe shaped a world unlike any other, giving it the most extreme seasons in our solar system. So next time you think about summer vacation, spare a thought for Uranus – it's having a very, very long one!
